text: The Nasdaq fell 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.7%, putting the S&P 500 and Dow in a correction (more than 10% off their highs) as chipmakers led an AI sell-off; Nvidia lost 14%.
The VIX jumped 26% to close at 35.89, its highest close since late March, after briefly touching 40.
Gold touched $3,502.93, its lowest in over a year, before ending US trading near $3,538, down about 2.4% on the day and on track for its worst week since March; silver fell about 3.8% to near $41.12.
Gold miners and silver funds fell harder than the metals: GDX closed down 5.0% at $68.40 and SLV down 6.7% at $36.97.
QQQ closed down 5.7% at $608.45, while the inverse SQQQ rose about 16.5%.
Treasury yields fell sharply as investors moved into bonds: the 10-year closed near 4.94% and the 2-year near 4.65%, even as traders still price about a 92% chance of a December Fed hike.
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since July, reaching about $57,650.
Brent edged up 0.6% to settle at $92.57 on Middle East tensions, but still posted a third straight weekly loss.
